Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
Foreign manpower and workplace laws

The Fair Consideration Framework, EP salary criteria and foreign manpower tightening levelled the playing field, while WICA and WSHA were enhanced for wage changes and workplace accidents.

  1. s00001 · 938Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    At the policy front, the Fair Consideration Framework and raising of Employment Pass (EP) salary criteria and other foreign manpower tightening measures have helped level the playing field for the local workforce.

  2. s00002 · 938Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    Enhancements to the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) and Workplace Safety and Health Act (WSHA) have also been instituted to keep pace with wage changes and workplace accidents.

Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
Review of Singapore labour laws

MOM and tripartite partners are suggested to review the EA, IRA, ECA and Trade Unions Act, including whether to restrict EA scope to those earning under $4,500 and exclude civil servants.

  1. s00008 · 938Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coastcontext

    The new nature of the employment relationship, rising median wages, workforce profile change and diversity of work will require us to review our labour legislation to keep pace with the changes and the uncertain global outlook.

  2. s00009 · 938Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    I am, therefore, suggesting for MOM and our tripartite partners to continue its good work to carry out a review of the labour laws of Singapore − the EA, IRA, Employment Claims Act (ECA) and Trade Unions Act − to keep pace with the changes.

  4. s00011 · 938Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    First is whether there is a need to restrict the scope of EA to those earning less than $4,500 as well as exclude civil servants from the ambit of the Act.

Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
Transfers under section 18A EA

With more mergers, acquisitions and restructuring, there is a challenge whether a transfer falls within section 18A of the EA, which allows transfer without retrenchment benefits.

  1. s00016 · 938Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    Third, with an increasing number of mergers and acquisitions and organisational restructuring and reorganisation these days, we often face the challenge of whether a transfer falls squarely within the provisions of section 18A of the EA which allows for transfer of employees to a new entity without the need to pay retrenchment benefits.

Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan · Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
Freelancers joining trade unions

The Trade Unions Act requires a contract of service to join a union, so freelancers on contracts for service may not be full members; a workgroup is suggested to study relaxing this.

  1. s00036 · 938Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    With greater complexity in the terms and conditions of work as well as cases of unfair termination of contract where workers, especially PMEs, are just given notice pay and told to leave the company, I hope the Act can keep pace with the developments and address some of these issues which may not be salary-related.

  3. s00038 · 938Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    At present, the Trade Unions Act requires a person to be in a "contract of service" to join a trade union.

  4. s00039 · 938Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    Freelancers who are in a "contract for service" may not be full-fledged union members per se.

  5. s00040 · 938Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    As such, I suggest MOM form a workgroup to study this carefully and remove or relax the prohibition and explore ways to allow freelancers to be union members without compromising or contravening traditional collective bargaining and representation.

  7. s00042 · 938Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    The review cannot be done in silos and, in the spirit of tripartism, I ask for our tripartite partners to review and examine carefully and further strengthen our tripartite relationship in the course of doing so by bringing even more workers and companies within our fold.

  8. s00043 · 938Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo — East Coast

    If we do not align our manpower with our economic growth strategies, given Singapore's tight labour market, manpower will become a bottleneck to economic growth.
